featured_reviews.name: ARYAN NAYAK
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am giving this college 1 star only because of the visiting faculty. I completed just my first year of undergrad here and then changed college — which turned out to be the best decision.

This college was a horrible experience, especially because of the staff and the coordinator. They are not strict — they are rude, inhuman, and extremely egoistic for no reason. It functions exactly like a typical government college. A colossal waste of time. I’m genuinely grateful I left when I did.

I have had strict teachers in school, but they were always polite and professional. Here, the main faculty and staff were openly rude. I had some pending documentation work (which shouldn’t have been required since I was already a student). I went two days later, was told it wouldn’t be done, and still showed up every day at the HOD’s office for two weeks between 12–5 PM. I apologized formally with a signed letter. I traveled 2 hours every day just to get this sorted, and the HOD literally slammed the door in my face everytime . I was just 18 years old.

Thankfully, I changed colleges within two weeks after that. It was a completely toxic environment.

Lectures were scheduled from 12–5 PM, but after traveling 2 hours to attend, we would often be informed that the lectures were cancelled. There was no way to give feedback because of the extremely rude and egoistic HOD. Even parents of first-year students noticed how arrogant and disrespectful the HOD was.

The staff was horrible — lazy, unhelpful, and irresponsible. Nothing was ever done on time. Getting just one signature for a basic document from the principal (who comes every day) took an entire month because of the staff and they still did not do it . When I approached the principal’s assistant, he told me I could meet her anytime she was free. I went and the principal signed it in five minutes. The problem was clearly the staff and hod's, not the principal.

When I went to get my leaving certificate signed, another HOD(Senior one) taunted me about restarting somewhere else. I simply said it was better to leave a toxic environment, and it truly was. The college I eventually graduated from was actually good, and I am so glad I escaped this place as soon as possible.

Let’s ignore the staff, but the main coordinators will say harsh words that will break your self-confidence.

When I had left the college and just came to complete last formalities the Senior hod exactly said, " Restarting again, it’s such a waste of time, waste of everything." Imagine this one reply coming from the main hod a complete toxic environment.
The HOD are not strict, they are rude, ruthless, merciless and we have to beg for everything.

Fortunately, most of my first year was during COVID, so I was saved from experiencing more of this chaos — except for the last two months, which were enough to show me how bad things were.

Please do not enroll in any course here, especially not management courses. They will make you suffer.

The only good thing about this college was the visiting faculty. They were excellent, understood our concerns, and genuinely tried to help — but they had no authority since it was a government college. I realized the truth the hard way, after going through two miserable months. Even the student crowd wasn’t much of an issue — 99% of the problems came from the HOD and staff.

Fortunately, I got a lot time after joining my new college and with their support did a lot of things and upskilled my experience and myself.

A tip for recently 12th grade pass, please if you do not get into any college, take a gap but do not enroll here, this college will leave you mentally disturbed. I have faced it. It took a full 4 months for me to recover.

For BMS do not even enroll. Only if you are planning to study abroad or in another city next year and don't want to waste a year then for time pass you can enroll because literally that is the only thing that is done.

Horrible management

I studied BScIT (Hons) here and graduated in 2013 — and it's been a dozen years, but Xavier's is my forever for me.

Late Perrie ma'am — HOD BMM, technically not my teacher — taught us EVS, but I'd call it 'life.' Her classes, her words, her book and film recommendations sparked something in me that led me to media and to reading far beyond what I was assigned.

This college has a mixed reputation that prospective students should carefully evaluate before taking admission. Despite the hype surrounding its legacy name and CET cut-offs, the actual academic and campus experience often falls short.
Faculty quality is highly inconsistent. While a few professors are genuinely knowledgeable and supportive, many follow outdated teaching methods, are frequently absent, or lack understanding of current industry practices. There is significant academic misguidance, and in several cases, students are better off learning independently than being taught incorrect or irrelevant information.
Teacher politics is a serious issue. Internal favoritism, ego-driven behavior, and power dynamics often affect academic decisions, evaluations, and student growth. Instead of mentorship, some faculty members prioritize authority over learning, which creates an unhealthy academic environment.
Infrastructure and maintenance are poor for an institution of this stature. Washrooms frequently lack basic necessities such as functional door knobs, proper water systems, and cleanliness. Broken facilities and poor upkeep are common across the campus, reflecting a lack of accountability.
There is no formal or structured placement system. While the college does host events and benefits from being located in India’s commercial hub, any industry exposure or opportunities usually come from personal networking rather than institutional support.
On the positive side, students value the hands-on learning culture, exposure through events, peer-driven growth, and the advantage of studying in Mumbai, which offers access to studios, firms, and creative networks.
However, outdated teaching approaches, internal politics, poor infrastructure, and lack of clear guidance make this college a risky choice. If you can afford a well-run private college with updated curriculum, better facilities, and transparent academic systems, it may be a better investment.
Do not fall for the hype, rankings, or legacy reputation alone. Thorough research is essential before committing your crucial design education years here.

Suggestion- Before selecting this college, students do personally visit the campus, evaluate basic necessities like washrooms and infrastructure, assess the teaching staff’s mindset, and research carefully before committing.

The university operates primarily from two campuses: the Fort Campus, known for its historic Rajabai Clock Tower, and the expansive Kalina Campus, which spans 243 acres and provides a serene environment conducive to learning and research.  ￼

Students have access to comprehensive facilities, including separate hostels for boys and girls, well-furnished rooms, spacious classrooms, and full-time internet connectivity.  The Jawaharlal Nehru Library serves as a central resource, housing an extensive collection of academic materials.  ￼ ￼

The university has produced notable alumni who have significantly contributed to various fields. However, some students have expressed concerns regarding placement opportunities, citing limited campus recruitment and lower salary packages.  Despite these challenges, the University of Mumbai remains a prominent educational institution, blending historical significance with academic diversity. ￼

featured_reviews.review_text:
I studied in the IT Department (Annex Building) of Maharashtra College, and the experience was extremely poor. The main problem is the management. Teachers like Saima Shaikh and Arun Shaikh, who are also involved in management work, rarely conducted proper lectures. Most of the time they just shared PDFs on WhatsApp and expected students to complete practicals without any teaching or guidance.

We barely had any proper classes. Many lectures were cancelled, teachers were absent, or they simply walked in to “check progress” instead of actually teaching. Basic management tasks are handled poorly even finding a classroom took 15–20 minutes every lecture

On the other hand, teachers like Ismail Sir, Shahid Sir, and a few others genuinely want to teach and support students, but even they look frustrated because the system around them is so unorganized. Important information about exams, submissions, and practicals was also mismanaged.

Overall, the IT department’s management needs serious improvement. Good teachers are trying, but the poor administration is affecting everyone.
